user_scenario:
You are Frank Hostetter, the son of Eleanor M. Hostetter and the person named as her representative on her paperwork at Keystone Ridge's Mechanicsburg center. You are calling the business office on a weekday afternoon from your desk at work, a little rushed but polite, careful with numbers and someone who prefers to hear things explained plainly.

Your mother went into the hospital at the beginning of October, came back to the center on Medicare a few days later, and Medicare stopped covering her stay about a week after that; she is staying on as a long-term resident and is paying privately again. You understand that now that she is back on private pay her security deposit has to be brought up to what the center requires, and you want to pay whatever deposit is owed today so it is settled. That is the one thing you are calling to do. You open by saying that, and you give your mother's full name, Eleanor M. Hostetter.

When the agent asks you to confirm who she is, you give her date of birth, November 2, 1937 (1937-11-02), and the last four digits of her Social Security number, 2618. Only if the agent asks for more do you add that she is in room 236-B now, that your phone is 717-555-0274 and your email is frank.hostetter@comcast.net. Only if the agent asks about her room do you mention that the family asked for her to move into a semi-private room on October 1 to keep costs down. Only if the agent asks about the hospital stay do you say she was taken to Holy Spirit on the morning of October 2, that you did not ask the center to keep her bed that day, and that the next afternoon you signed to hold it until she came back on October 5. Only if the agent asks about other time away do you say she spent two nights at your house in Camp Hill around October 17 and that you asked them to keep her bed. Only if the agent asks about insurance do you say her long-term care insurance policy pays the center directly under an assignment and that you do not know the daily figure. Only if the agent asks about her extras do you say she has the in-room phone, had cable until you stopped it in July, has had an oxygen concentrator in her room since mid-August, and now and then has a manicure or a haircut at the center or has guests to lunch. If the agent asks whether you also want to pay her October bill today, you say no, you will deal with the bills when the next statement comes, and today you only want the deposit taken care of.

If the agent explains that something on her account has to be put right or entered before the deposit can be worked out, you say that is fine and that they should go ahead and do it; you do not ask for the details and you do not suggest what it might be. You do not know any of the figures yourself and never offer one. If the agent tells you a deposit amount, you accept it. You want to pay it by electronic bank transfer (ACH) from your checking account, the same way you have paid her monthly bills, and you say so when the agent asks how you will pay. When the agent hands you the payment step, you make the deposit payment yourself with the agreement reference number and the amount the agent gives you, choosing ACH, and you read back the receipt it returns if asked. Once the payment has gone through, you thank the agent and end the call.

design_rationale:
# Task 1 dossier — private_pay_residency_billing (private billing resumes after a Medicare Part A stay) — round 9

## 1. Why this is a good test
Frank Hostetter only asks to pay the security deposit owed now that his mother is billed privately again after Medicare. The figure rests on two corrections nobody mentions: the October advance was posted 2026-09-25 at the private room, before her move to a semi-private room on 2026-10-01 and before the Part A conversion was recorded, so it still bills October to the resident although she left for hospital on 2026-10-02 and was on Part A from 2026-10-05; and the days after Medicare's liability ended were never charged again. The resumption deposit is not worked out until the agreement carries the re-charge span, and the re-charge counts only once the advance carries its payer-conversion credit.

## 2. Scope snapshot
Draw: task 1 prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,4,6]. Claimed: private_ext_conversion_credit (6), private_ext_resumed_recharge (4), private_ext_resumption_deposit (6, user root). The move (2026-10-01) is dated before the recorded conversion date 2026-10-11, which falls inside the advance's span, so the room-change credit and the new-room span owe nothing: the payer-conversion credit gives the advance back (with the cheaper-room difference for the moved day before the stay) and the re-charge charges the new tier. The additional deposit does not apply (a conversion is recorded).

## 3. Problem-tree card
Chain conversion credit -> re-charge span -> resumption deposit (user root); state form, value_input.
- re-charge <- conversion (rc_days): "The span re-charging the days after the other payer source's coverage ended is posted only after the advance charge billed for those days carries its payer-conversion credit." Skip: 0.00 (nothing posted); deposit 2,722.67.
- resumption deposit <- re-charge (r_tier): "The resumption deposit is not worked out until the agreement carries the span re-charging the days after the other payer source's coverage ended." Skip: 2,722.67 instead of 1,012.67.

## 4. Factor cards (tier -> standard-method figure)
Conversion credit 13,088.00: first_converted_day_rule (m, cross medicare, multi-source) coverage start 10-05 (standard recorded date: 10,472.00); hospital_days_rule (m, cross bedhold) the departure 10-02 on the hospital reservation begun on the qualifying admission date -> 3 hospital days (standard no hospital day: 11,924.00); moved_day_rate_rule (p) semi-private 38.00 cheaper than the posted private room on the current schedule (standard none: 13,050.00); credit_tier_rule (p) Private, the tier the charge was posted for (standard 11,948.00); credit_schedule_rule (p) current (standard 12,638.00); netted_step_rule (m) 15.00 schedule gap (standard the charge's daily rate: 12,246.00). The hospital days are one quantity (the days away before coverage, whatever the hold), read from the departure on the hospital reservation begun on the qualifying admission date or returned on the coverage start (any kind and status), else on the resident's only hospital reservation, or, with none on file, from the inpatient admission; where none of these reads applies the policy credits the base way, from the first day the other payer source took over; the netted and moved days follow the first credited day itself.
Re-charge 6,368.00: recharge_start_rule (m, cross medicare, multi-source) late ABN 10-14 (standard 7,562.00); recharge_leave_rule (m, cross bedhold) 2 booked, none reversed (standard 7,164.00); recharge_tier_rule (p) Semi-Private, move dated before the recorded conversion date (standard 6,976.00); recharge_schedule_rule (p) current (standard 6,144.00).
Resumption deposit 1,012.67: resumption_days_rule (p) 45 (standard 0.00); resumption_tier_rule (p) Semi-Private (standard 2,722.67); resumption_schedule_rule (p) current (standard 382.67); resumption_insurer_rule (m) 3,000 / 30 = 100.00 (standard 5,512.67); r_recurring_allowance_rule (m, cross ancillary) oxygen first charged in the window -> latest service month 214.00 (standard 1,054.67); r_item_allowance_rule (m, cross ancillary) three items 56.00 / 3 = 18.67 (standard 994.00).

## 6. Pairwise method-tier table (XF-7)
- notice_anchor: whole span / days before delivery + notice days / days before the schedule date (three window ends, each from a different record).
- leave_kind, span_leave_rule, recharge_leave_rule: booked resident-private days less the days reversed against that booking (recorded counts) / days held so far on a hold in force with nothing booked (date difference to today) / none.
- move_date_source: the date named by the latest request (request record + tariff comparison of the two tiers) / the span's first day / the recorded move date.
- netting_rule (room change): late-notice credit's netted days at its amount per day plus any billing-error credit's netted days at the charge's rate / billing-error credit's netted days at the charge's rate / nothing.
- span_start_rule: the room-change credit's own days from its first day (recorded count) / the whole span / recorded move date to span end (date difference).
- first_converted_day_rule: later of Part A coverage start and span start / span start / later of recorded conversion date and span start.
- hospital_days_rule: first hospital day from the stay's departure (hospital reservation begun on the qualifying admission, or returned on the coverage start, or the only one by count; any kind and status; midnight census) / from the qualifying inpatient admission (no hospital reservation) / no hospital day.
- moved_day_rate_rule: posted tier's current rate less the agreement tier's (cheaper move) / posted tier's current rate less the isolation billing tier's (isolation placement) / none.
- netted_step_rule: schedule gap (two tariff inputs) / credits total / their days (ledger sums) / the charge's daily rate (recorded rate).
- recharge_start_rule: from the ABN delivery date / no day (review pending) / from the recorded conversion date.
- insurer_benefit_rule, resumption_insurer_rule: latest payment / its charge's days / three-month total / averaging days / nothing.
- recurring allowance: three-month total / 3 (every service charged before the window and in the latest month) / the latest service month's charges / price-schedule month per service billed in twelve months (tariff input).
- item allowance: three-month total / 3 / the latest item charge / nothing.
